newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-News says U.S. Q1 results up 7.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News says U.S. Q1 results up 7.0 pct.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's global media group, The News Corp Ltd, said on Tuesday that operating income for the first quarter was flat on the same quarter a year ago, with a strengthening of the Australian dollar masking a seven percent rise in U.S. dollar operating results.
News Corp earlier reported first quarter pre-abnormals net profits fell to A$285 million from A$284 million. Operating income was A$378 million versus A$377 million a year earlier.
"A strengthening of the Australian dollar masked the seven percent improvement in U.S. dollar operating results," News said.
"Contributing to that improvement was the worldwide box office success of Independence Day, as well as marked gains in profitability at U.K. newspapers and book publishing," News Corp said.
"Offsetting these gains were weaker results in U.S. television, Australian newspapers and book publishing, which lacked results from the educational division which was sold in March 1996," it said.
Income from associated companies was affected by gains at BSkyB, Australian Newsprint Mills and Independent Newspapers Ltd, News Corp said.
There was also a positive contribution from the FOX/Liberty Sports joint venture, it said.
"Losses at Ansett Australia however produced reduced results," the company said.
Analysts had forecast pre-abnormals first quarter net profit would be around A$320 million to A$330 million, up around 14 percent from the A$284 million recorded in the first quarter of 1995/96.
